scope: Three art directions with scene, 2D background and foreground prop-design sheets; user confirmed Unity implementation follows selection.

variants.name: 苔墙拾镜
variants.hook: 破镜片、粗树根与苔绿石墙，接近草图的荒园气质。
variants.reflector: 碎裂的旧镜片，嵌在残留黄铜小框中
variants.design: DIRECTION A — MOSS WALL AND FOUND MIRROR. Match the user's sketch most closely. Palette: deep muted moss green overhead, smoke-blue shade, pearl-grey wall, small warm ochre / terracotta accents. A massive tree root curls over rough old stonework. The abandoned planting trough is a low uneven stone enclosure covered with soft moss and a few tiny orange flowers. The wall opening is a natural broken triangular crack in stone. The reflector is ONE irregular triangular shard from a discarded old mirror, held in a surviving slim tarnished-brass fragment frame with a small vertical swivel pin, anchored in a squat cracked stone/wood support among clay fragments. It must read immediately as a silver mirror surface with one controlled white glint; keep edge cracks only, do not split its functioning face into many separate pieces. A small root wrapped around the base suggests it has been there a long time, but the face and knob remain free to turn. Right-hand steps are uneven thick stone slabs bridged by tree roots, with a clear small opening beneath the edge; a living pearl-grey scale is visible inside it. Quiet, slightly lonely, soft reclaimed nature. Maintain the user's tiny spirit scale and compact near-ground puzzle.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE complete game-camera concept screenshot for Level 01 "Mossy Threshold", one of three selectable art directions for a Unity 2.5D orthographic puzzle game.
REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 is the user's rough scene sketch: STRICT reference for environmental scale, overall composition, spatial proportions and camera. Image 2 is ONLY the identity of the tiny playable light-spirit; do NOT copy Image 2's composition or enlarge the character.
CAMERA / SCALE: match the Image 1 moderately wide landscape frame, approximately 3:2. A fixed orthographic camera looking slightly down at about 15–20 degrees, almost side-on into a shallow stage with some ground depth; no perspective convergence, no dramatic isometric bird's-eye view. Enormous wall and densely overhanging tree canopy fill the upper roughly 65–70% of the frame. The accessible foreground path occupies the lower roughly 25–30%. The ONE playable character must be VERY SMALL, only 3–4 percent of the full image height, standing near lower center-left at around x=37%, y=88%. This scale is crucial: the garden is gigantic to the tiny spirit.
COMPOSITION anchored to the sketch: partial tall wrought iron garden gate cropped at far LEFT with low entry steps below it. A high weathered boundary wall across the back, overgrown trees and vines above. A low abandoned planting trough / flowerbed at lower-left-middle. A shaded exterior building corner / wall mass frames the RIGHT edge, not an interior room. A narrow broken opening in the boundary wall near x=45%, y=48% admits one small controlled shaft of sunshine. A clear continuous walkable mossy threshold path runs from the left entry across the bottom, then follows a crack toward an overturned terracotta flowerpot near x=85%, y=83%, the next-level entrance. The plant pot is physically UPSIDE-DOWN with its base uppermost and a small chipped gap at its bottom rim.
SINGLE REFLECTION PUZZLE, READABLE: one and ONLY ONE rotatable reflective object near x=51%, y=75%, standing amongst a few old garden scraps. It is about 1.5–2 times the spirit's height, with a distinct upright pivot / little turn handle the spirit can reach. Fixed mounting inclination is allowed, with rotation around a vertical pivot. The broken-wall opening, reflector and target are simultaneously visible. Show one straight thin incoming golden light shaft from the wall opening to the CENTER of the reflecting face, and ONE straight reflected ray traveling from that exact center toward x=73%, y=80%. There is a single angular bend at the mirror surface; no other turns, curved beams, extra mirrors or lasers. Both beam corridors are empty and unobstructed. Use a slightly broad translucent warm shaft but a readable narrow bright core; do not flood the scene with haze.
TARGET: at x=73%, y=80%, a VERY SMALL grey-white stone-like living tail-tip scale is partly buried UNDER the edge of broken mossy stone steps. These steps have an OPEN SIDE GAP facing toward the reflector, so the beam enters the exposed side gap and hits the scale directly, never passes through stone. Show only a tiny cropped local patch of the creature, approximately 5–7% of image width, not a whole animal, face, paw or long tail. The living patch resembles a softly rounded chalky stone at first, with delicate scale contours and a faint pale turquoise / warm ivory inner glow. In this selected screenshot it has just received light: the contact point gently brightens, but the creature remains mostly buried.
CHARACTER: one tiny large-headed ivory-blue light spirit with a compact short body, little drop-shaped limbs, a swept pointed glowing stardust head crest, small dark eyes and gold chest core; based on reference Image 2. Tiny scale, clearly placed on the foreground ground. No extra characters or full food-light beast.
ART DIRECTION: delicate artistic FAIRYTALE WATERCOLOR ILLUSTRATION, translucent broad washes, beautiful lost-and-found watercolor edges, visible paper pigment granulation, selective fine ink contour, restrained warm sunlight against cool shaded greens/blues, intimate illustrated-panel atmosphere inspired by Gorogoa. 2D painted appearance even though foreground volumes could be built in 3D. NO photorealism, 3D-render gloss, realistic grass noise, painterly oil impasto or dense game-asset texture.
GAMEPLAY FOREGROUND LINEWORK: playable floor silhouette, entry-step edges, reflector and turn handle, target-side step opening and overturned pot must have clear continuous deep charcoal / muted umber ink outlines, about 2–3 pixels at a 1536-pixel-wide image. Selective inner seams clarify the walkable surface and collisions. Ground and interactive props are visibly more sharply defined than the background. Background wall/trees use soft low-contrast painted edges, NO equally heavy outlines on every leaf or background stone. Keep an empty visual breathing corridor around the reflector and between reflector and target.
NO text, title, HUD, arrows, numbered labels, annotations, comparison panels, foreground object closeups or frames. This is one finished full-scene illustration, not a collage.

variants.name: 旧圃铜光
variants.hook: 温暖砖墙与规整花圃，反射物来自废弃植物名牌。
variants.reflector: 铜质植物名牌经过磨亮的平整背面
variants.design: DIRECTION B — OLD BRICK PLANTING COURT AND POLISHED BRASS LABEL. Keep the reference's scale and functional positions, but change the actual architecture: a low rectangular red-brick planting bed with rounded coping stones, orderly brick entry steps, a damaged curved arch fragment within the high garden wall, and sparse trailing nasturtium vines. The dense canopy still encloses the top, but warm pale terracotta, dusty apricot and sage green replace the moss-grey stone palette. A small broken gap in the brick arch/wall admits the same single sunshaft. The ONE reflective object is an OLD FLAT BRASS BOTANICAL LABEL mounted on a short rotatable iron pin: its smooth BACK SIDE has been rubbed bright like a mirror, with a clean pale reflected stripe and a distinct dark outlined rim; no engraved lettering faces the camera. It is a small softly rounded rectangle tilted at a fixed mounting angle but swiveling around the pin, with a reachable little lever below; do not draw it as a dull sign or curved scoop. Neighboring scraps are matte so only this back surface glints. The target sits in an open gap below two displaced brick-and-stone threshold steps at the right; expose the small stone-like living scale. One upside-down weathered terracotta nursery pot beyond it marks the exit. Gentle, cared-for long ago, warm fairytale memory. Do not turn the low planting bed into a giant central fountain or change the tiny character scale.

variants.name: 藤影残灯
variants.hook: 蓝灰墙柱与垂藤，旧园灯的反光片引导第一束光。
variants.reflector: 旧园灯遗落的平面镀银反光片
variants.design: DIRECTION C — IVY SHADE AND FALLEN GARDEN-LANTERN REFLECTOR. Retain the layout and immense scale but use a different architectural rhythm: tall narrow blue-grey stone pilasters, thin vertical ivy shadows, a scalloped low stone planting trough and slender ferns; distant wall and tree layers dissolve into lavender-grey mist. Overhead canopy is broad and dark but drawn with restrained watercolor shapes. A missing narrow wall-stone near the middle releases the same warm focused sunshaft. The ONE reflective object is a FLAT SILVERED REFLECTOR PANEL salvaged from an old small garden lantern: an irregular narrow trapezoid still held by one side of its simple oxidized metal bracket, a tiny intact vertical swivel pivot and clear reachable knob. A few matte broken lantern-frame pieces sit beside its base, but NO lit bulb, active lantern flame, extra shiny glass panes or implied lamp-lighting puzzle. The panel is flat and clearly mirror-like, not a parabolic bowl. The building corner on the right is a tall plain darker stone mass framing a moss-covered threshold stair, with the small open side gap containing the pale living tail scale. The overturned flowerpot is charcoal-edged and muted burnt orange, a soft final accent. Meditative, airy blue shadow and silver light, with amber sun. One clear reflection, subtle background, unmistakable inked foreground.
